FIXED at the root: the publisher now repairs the queue before it sends. Root cause was ownership -- the producers write the placeholder on a captioner failure, the post queues like any other, and the repair was opt-in (APPLY=1), so the artifact published verbatim unless a human intervened. bin/scheduled_posting.sh now runs 'captions:refresh_placeholders APPLY=1 INCLUDE_DUE=1' ahead of scheduling:post_scheduled, non-fatally (a captioner outage publishes as before and this check keeps the condition open). PlaceholderRefresh also gained include_due: the old future-only predicate skipped exactly the rows a late tick is about to publish, which is the hole this guard exists to close. Verified: 5 queued placeholders refreshed in production with 0 failures (333/334/335/336/337, model gemma3:4b, statuses unchanged; pre-repair captions backed up to ops/backups/placeholder_captions.20260920T053637Z.json); DB now shows 0 unpublished placeholders; the next probe auto-closed this entry; rspec spec/services/caption_generation 6/0 and full suite 383/0. NOTE FOR TIM: this is a policy change -- a queued caption is now replaced automatically instead of waiting for APPLY=1. The placeholder is a failure artifact, not content, so publishing it was the worse default; revert is one line in bin/scheduled_posting.sh.
